fichas.title: Superyacht marinas
fichas.summary: Superyacht marinas need extensive berthing space, deep water, substantial utilities, and service comparable to a five-star hotel. Planning should separate owner and crew/service areas and provide security, emergency planning, and environmentally responsible operation.
uses: Supplying electricity, fresh water, waste-water pump-out, and fuel

fichas.title: Marina security and sustainability
fichas.summary: Marina security combines active measures, such as visible berth arrangements and alarms, with surveillance, lighting, patrols, emergency plans, and security management. Marinas should provide emergency training and reduce environmental impacts through efficient energy use, alternative energy, safe materials, and operational zoning.
uses: Protecting boats, equipment, and people from natural hazards and criminal activity
Managing emergency response and staff training
Reducing energy use and preventing water and subsoil pollution
furniture_equipment: Geothermal, wind, waterpower, photovoltaic, and solar-heating systems

fichas.title: Marina clubhouse functional scheme
fichas.summary: The functional scheme organizes marina clubhouse spaces across lower and upper ground floors, with a boat house and entrance hall connecting activity, service, and public areas. The diagram includes changing and wash facilities, boat-related work and storage rooms, club spaces, administration, and guest accommodation.
spaces: Drying room for sails and clothes
uses: Storing and maintaining boats, sails, tools, and equipment
